  "claims": [
    {"id":"f1","concept_id":"c1","text":"A checkpoint moves transactions from the WAL back into the original database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a \" checkpoint \".","pass":0},
    {"id":"f2","concept_id":"c2","text":"sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers automatic checkpointing after a commit when the WAL contains N or more frames.","source_id":"S3","quote":"automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f3","concept_id":"c2","text":"Passing N equal to zero or a negative value to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f4","concept_id":"c2","text":"Each new database connection enables automatic checkpointing with a default threshold of 1000 pages or the SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT setting.","source_id":"S3","quote":"Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f5","concept_id":"c3","text":"Registering a callback with sqlite3_wal_hook() disables automatic checkpointing configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint().","source_id":"S3","quote":"Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f6","concept_id":"c4","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for database readers or writers to finish.","source_id":"S2","quote":"Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f7","concept_id":"c4","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.","source_id":"S2","quote":"The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f8","concept_id":"c5","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL invokes the busy handler while waiting for no database writer and for all readers to use the most recent database snapshot.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f9","concept_id":"c5","text":"While pending, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL blocks new database writers but allows new database readers.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f10","concept_id":"c6","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART adds a wait after FULL-style checkpointing until all readers read only from the database file.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f11","concept_id":"c6","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART ensures that the next writer restarts the WAL from the beginning.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f12","concept_id":"c7","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation of the WAL to zero bytes immediately before a successful return to RESTART behavior.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f13","concept_id":"c8","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and serves to retrieve pnLog and pnCkpt values.","source_id":"S2","quote":"This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f14","concept_id":"c9","text":"A checkpoint running concurrently with readers must stop when it reaches a WAL page past any current reader's end mark.","source_id":"S1","quote":"A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f15","concept_id":"c9","text":"The checkpoint records progress in the wal-index and resumes from that point on its next invocation.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f16","concept_id":"c10","text":"Continuously overlapping active readers can prevent checkpoints from completing and allow unbounded WAL growth.","source_id":"S1","quote":"if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f17","concept_id":"c10","text":"Checkpoint starvation can be avoided by attempting checkpoints during reader gaps when no processes read the database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are \"reader gaps\": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f18","concept_id":"c11","text":"A writer rewinds the WAL when its entire contents have been transferred and synced to the database and no readers use the WAL.","source_id":"S1","quote":"if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning","pass":0},
    {"id":"f19","concept_id":"c12","text":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpointing moves its content into the database.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database","pass":0},
    {"id":"f20","concept_id":"c12","text":"The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.","source_id":"S1","quote":"and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL. Checkpoint also requires more seeking.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f21","concept_id":"c13","text":"By default, the thread performing the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit also runs the automatic checkpoint.","source_id":"S1","quote":"By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f22","concept_id":"c13","text":"With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.","source_id":"S1","quote":"Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).","pass":0},
    {"id":"f23","concept_id":"c14","text":"Concurrent checkpoint-lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f24","concept_id":"c14","text":"If the busy handler returns zero before obtaining the writer lock or while waiting for readers, the checkpoint continues with PASSIVE behavior.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE","pass":0},
    {"id":"f25","concept_id":"c14","text":"A checkpoint that falls back to PASSIVE behavior after the busy handler returns zero returns SQLITE_BUSY.","source_id":"S2","quote":"checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f26","concept_id":"c15","text":"When pnLog is non-NULL, it receives the total WAL frame count, or -1 if an error or non-WAL database prevents checkpoint execution.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file or to -1 if the checkpoint could not run because of an error or because the database is not in WAL mode","pass":0},
    {"id":"f27","concept_id":"c15","text":"pnCkpt counts all checkpointed frames in the WAL, including frames checkpointed before the current call.","source_id":"S2","quote":"*pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)","pass":0},
    {"id":"f28","concept_id":"c15","text":"Successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE sets both pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to zero.","source_id":"S2","quote":"Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f29","concept_id":"c16","text":"A NULL or empty zDb makes sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 attempt the operation on every attached WAL database.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f30","concept_id":"c16","text":"When checkpointing all attached WAL databases, SQLITE_BUSY on one database does not prevent attempts on the remaining databases.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f31","concept_id":"c16","text":"An error other than SQLITE_BUSY while processing an attached database immediately abandons further processing and returns that error.","source_id":"S2","quote":"If any other error occurs while processing an attached database, processing is abandoned and the error code is returned to the caller immediately.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f32","concept_id":"c17","text":"The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.","source_id":"S1","quote":"A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f33","concept_id":"c2","text":"Checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by automatic checkpointing use PASSIVE mode.","source_id":"S1","quote":"All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f34","concept_id":"c14","text":"SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART, and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE acquire an exclusive writer lock in addition to the checkpoint lock.","source_id":"S2","quote":"The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive \"writer\" lock on the database file.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f35","concept_id":"c12","text":"With synchronous=NORMAL and checkpointing in another thread or process, transactions may roll back after a power failure or hard reset.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The downside to this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.","pass":0},
    {"id":"f36","concept_id":"c11","text":"A checkpoint normally recycles the WAL without truncating it unless journal_size_limit is set.","source_id":"S1","quote":"The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.","pass":0}

claims.text: A checkpoint moves transactions from the WAL back into the original database.
claims.quote: Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a " checkpoint ".

claims.text: sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers automatic checkpointing after a commit when the WAL contains N or more frames.
claims.quote: automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.

claims.text: Passing N equal to zero or a negative value to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.
claims.quote: Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.

claims.text: Each new database connection enables automatic checkpointing with a default threshold of 1000 pages or the SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT setting.
claims.quote: Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.

claims.text: Registering a callback with sqlite3_wal_hook() disables automatic checkpointing configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint().
claims.quote: Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for database readers or writers to finish.
claims.quote: Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.
claims.quote: The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL invokes the busy handler while waiting for no database writer and for all readers to use the most recent database snapshot.
claims.quote: This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot.

claims.text: While pending, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL blocks new database writers but allows new database readers.
claims.quote: This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART adds a wait after FULL-style checkpointing until all readers read only from the database file.
claims.quote: This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL with the addition that after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART ensures that the next writer restarts the WAL from the beginning.
claims.quote: This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE adds truncation of the WAL to zero bytes immediately before a successful return to RESTART behavior.
claims.quote: This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP checkpoints zero frames and serves to retrieve pnLog and pnCkpt values.
claims.quote: This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.

claims.text: A checkpoint running concurrently with readers must stop when it reaches a WAL page past any current reader's end mark.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.

claims.text: The checkpoint records progress in the wal-index and resumes from that point on its next invocation.
claims.quote: The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.

claims.text: Continuously overlapping active readers can prevent checkpoints from completing and allow unbounded WAL growth.
claims.quote: if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.text: Checkpoint starvation can be avoided by attempting checkpoints during reader gaps when no processes read the database.
claims.quote: This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.

claims.text: A writer rewinds the WAL when its entire contents have been transferred and synced to the database and no readers use the WAL.
claims.quote: if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning

claims.text: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before checkpointing moves its content into the database.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database

claims.text: The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.
claims.quote: and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL. Checkpoint also requires more seeking.

claims.text: By default, the thread performing the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit also runs the automatic checkpoint.
claims.quote: By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.

claims.text: With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.
claims.quote: Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).

claims.text: Concurrent checkpoint-lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler.
claims.quote: If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.

claims.text: If the busy handler returns zero before obtaining the writer lock or while waiting for readers, the checkpoint continues with PASSIVE behavior.
claims.quote: If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE

claims.text: A checkpoint that falls back to PASSIVE behavior after the busy handler returns zero returns SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.

claims.text: When pnLog is non-NULL, it receives the total WAL frame count, or -1 if an error or non-WAL database prevents checkpoint execution.
claims.quote: If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file or to -1 if the checkpoint could not run because of an error or because the database is not in WAL mode

claims.text: pnCkpt counts all checkpointed frames in the WAL, including frames checkpointed before the current call.
claims.quote: *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)

claims.text: Successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE sets both pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to zero.
claims.quote: Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.

claims.text: A NULL or empty zDb makes sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 attempt the operation on every attached WAL database.
claims.quote: If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.

claims.text: When checkpointing all attached WAL databases, SQLITE_BUSY on one database does not prevent attempts on the remaining databases.
claims.quote: If an SQLITE_BUSY error is encountered when processing one or more of the attached WAL databases, the operation is still attempted on any remaining attached databases and SQLITE_BUSY is returned at the end.

claims.text: An error other than SQLITE_BUSY while processing an attached database immediately abandons further processing and returns that error.
claims.quote: If any other error occurs while processing an attached database, processing is abandoned and the error code is returned to the caller immediately.

claims.text: The WAL cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can only complete when no other transactions are running, which means the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.

claims.text: Checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by automatic checkpointing use PASSIVE mode.
claims.quote: All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART, and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE acquire an exclusive writer lock in addition to the checkpoint lock.
claims.quote: The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive "writer" lock on the database file.

claims.text: With synchronous=NORMAL and checkpointing in another thread or process, transactions may roll back after a power failure or hard reset.
claims.quote: The downside to this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.

claims.text: A checkpoint normally recycles the WAL without truncating it unless journal_size_limit is set.
claims.quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.

limitations: The three supplied sources are official SQLite documentation from one origin; they do not satisfy a floor requiring independent source origins.
S2's dedicated API specification governs mode details: S1's three-mode summary omits TRUNCATE and NOOP.
For RESTART reader behavior, S2 explicitly says readers are not impeded; this takes precedence over S1's broader warning that RESTART and TRUNCATE might block readers.

S1's statement that checkpoints require no other transactions to complete is broader than S2's mode-specific reader conditions; only the supported consequence that an active write transaction prevents WAL reset is retained.
RESTART and TRUNCATE completion is conditional on successful execution; busy-handler termination can cause PASSIVE fallback and SQLITE_BUSY.
The bounded packet review does not establish research saturation, independent corroboration, unsupported history, or the origin of documentation differences.
The claim budget limits coverage; omitted API details and performance tradeoffs remain unassessed rather than disproved.
